extraction.name: Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images
extraction.description: A dataset of millions of tiny color images collected from the web for unsupervised training of deep generative models, with additional labeled subsets (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100) for object recognition experiments.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.citeAs: Krizhevsky, A. (2009). Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by colleagues at MIT and NYU over six months by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in the WordNet lexical database using several search engines (Google, Flickr, AltaVista). They kept roughly the first 3000 results for each search term, removed perfect duplicates and images with excessively large white portions, and assigned a rough label based on the search term.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the web using search engines (Google, Flickr, AltaVista) based on WordNet noun terms.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were downscaled to 32x32 pixels, duplicates were removed, and images with excessive white pixels were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were downscaled to 32x32 pixels, duplicates were removed, and images with excessive white pixels were filtered out. The dataset was whitened using ZCA whitening transformation to decorrelate pixel values and remove low-variance directions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human annotators were paid to label a subset of the dataset. Annotators were given a class and asked to examine all images found with that class as the search term, including images from hyponyms of the main search term. They were instructed to reject mislabeled images based on criteria such as photo-realism, single prominent object, and clear object identity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotators were paid a fixed sum per hour, and the authors personally verified every label submitted. Duplicate images were removed using L2 norm comparison.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases due to the nature of online image search technology and the search terms used. The rough labels from search terms are unreliable, and the dataset may not be representative of all natural images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to 32x32 pixel images, which may not capture fine details. The rough labels from search terms are unreliable, making it difficult to use for object recognition without additional labeling. The dataset may contain duplicates and synthetic figures.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and testing for unsupervised learning of deep generative models, object recognition experiments, and feature extraction for classification tasks.
